clue.text: Keep one's speed?

definitions.meaning: a keep is a castle stronghold, and a remote secure stronghold has this name
the quality of being quick, read as a noun formed from fast

explanation.surface: A runner is urged to hold their pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the castle-tower noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stronghold or retreat and, literally, swiftness.

clue.text: Maybe hanging country

definitions.meaning: a hanging ... is the scrap of card left dangling on a punched ballot paper, as in the 2000 Florida recount
a landlocked nation in north-central Africa

explanation.definitionFit: A partly punched ballot leaves a dangling scrap of that name; it is also an African nation.

clue.text: Force a way into the upper classes

parts.note: G stands for force, as in g-force
an entry is a way in to a place

explanation.surface: Someone muscles their way into high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the gentry are people of good social position just below the nobility.

clue.text: Please be serving cheese

indicators.note: the letters are dished up in a new arrangement, as food is served out differently

explanation.surface: A polite request to bring out the cheese course.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bel Paese is a mild, soft Italian cheese.

clue.text: Security after one gets into higher education?

indicators.note: the piece made from after and one goes inside the higher-education abbreviation

parts.note: COLL is an abbreviation for college
later means after
A is one, as the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A student is promised money once they win a university place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets into' signals a container; COLL is a standard abbreviation for college, standing in for higher education.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: collateral is property pledged as security for a loan.

clue.text: Old Bob was worth two of them

definitions.text: Old Bob was worth two of them

parts.words: Old Bob was worth two of them
parts.note: a bob was slang for the old shilling, worth twelve pence, so two coins of sixpence made one; it reads like a man called Bob

explanation.definitionFit: A tanner was British slang for the pre-decimal sixpence, half a shilling or bob.

clue.text: Hats off to county and central Asian city

indicators.note: the letters of the hat word are thrown off their usual order

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: Locals in an Asian city doff their caps to an English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges HATS into TASH; KENT is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

clue.text: Canter off in a dream

indicators.note: the letters of canter go off course into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider trots along half asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals that CANTER is rearranged; 'in a dream' matches 'in a trance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a trance is a dreamlike, half-conscious state.

clue.text: Backward boy, one without 10

indicators.note: the joined words for boy and one are read from right to left

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as the word one

explanation.surface: A slow child is described as lacking something.
explanation.definitionFit: Enodal means without nodes or knots, and a stud is a knob or boss, so the cross-reference fits loosely.

clue.text: Half the class are kept for propagation

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for the class is kept

parts.note: a class is made up of students

explanation.surface: Half a school class is held back for breeding purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half the' keeps the first four of the eight letters of STUDENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is an animal, usually a stallion, kept for breeding.

clue.text: Track over the river gives quite a bounce

indicators.note: the tram track goes over, or around, the river

parts.note: a tramline is a track for trams
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A railway bridge over a river gives a bumpy ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a trampoline is a sprung sheet that gives a big bounce.

clue.text: Every single one entered by the head

indicators.note: the word by is entered by the word for every single one

parts.note: taken as written
each means every single one

explanation.surface: Every pupil is visited by the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Beachy Head is a chalk headland on the Sussex coast of England, so this word goes with Head.

clue.text: Room can be found for plonk

parts.note: a chamber is a room
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Space can be made for cheap wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plonk' is British slang for cheap wine, used ironically of a grand burgundy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Chambertin is a red burgundy, so it is wine, here jokingly called plonk.

clue.text: Being that made cure rate unreliable

indicators.note: the letters of cure rate cannot be relied on to stay in place

explanation.surface: Something whose cure rate was unreliable, like a quack remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a being is any living creature.

clue.text: Bogus qualification in African culture

parts.note: sham means bogus
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree qualification

explanation.surface: A fake degree in African studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'culture' means cultivation here, not arts and customs.
explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa a shamba is a cultivated plot of land, a place of agriculture.

clue.text: A large number in crazy kerchiefs

indicators.note: the large number goes inside the word for crazy

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Lots of people are wearing wild headscarves.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bandanas are large patterned kerchiefs worn on the head or neck.

clue.text: Bride's shattering conclusion?

indicators.note: the letters of the bride word, with its s, break apart and are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A wedding ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering' rearranges BRIDES; the whole clue also describes the answer, what remains when something shatters.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered fragments left after something has been broken up.

clue.text: Indication for surgery — heart bypass, with modern operation

indicators.note: the middle of surgery is bypassed, leaving its first and last letters
the letters of modern are operated on and reworked

explanation.surface: A surgeon's notes on a heart bypass done by a modern method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart bypass' leaves S and Y from surgery; 'operation' rearranges MODERN into NDROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a set of symptoms that indicate a condition.

clue.text: Expression of grievance by one in factory

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the word for factory

parts.note: a plant is a factory
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A worker in a factory voices a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a plaint is a complaint or lament.

clue.text: Court interrupts hearing with refreshment

indicators.note: the refreshment breaks into the middle of the hearing

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in court
a bun is a light snack

explanation.surface: A judge halts proceedings for a tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tribunal is a court of justice or body that judges disputes.

clue.text: Bring back capital punishment?

parts.note: reads as a call to restore the death penalty, but means to hang something such as a picture again

explanation.definitionFit: To rehang is to hang again, as with a picture, which jokingly reads as reviving the noose.

clue.text: Dumb as the majority are reported to be?

definitions.meaning: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak

definitions.text: as the majority are reported to be?
definitions.meaning: the phrase ... majority describes the mass of people who hold views but do not voice them

explanation.definitionFit: Mute or saying nothing, and the description given to the quiet majority of a population.

clue.text: Tahini seems a paste

indicators.note: the letters of seems a are pounded to a paste and remade

explanation.surface: Tahini looks like a smooth spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paste' signals that SEEMSA is rearranged; the definition is by association, since tahini is ground from these seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahini is a Middle Eastern paste made from ground sesame seeds, so it stands for the seed here.

clue.text: Cleaners for prince without a princess

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the prince's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Charles was the Prince of Wales
Di is Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A prince seeks domestic help now his princess has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, which is what makes the surface's sad story misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Charladies are women employed to clean houses or offices.

clue.text: Wax well-meaning but righteous?

indicators.note: a righteous person is without sin, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: sincere means well-meaning or genuine

explanation.surface: Someone praises a person who means well but is self-righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Cere is the waxy skin at the base of a bird's bill, from the Latin word for wax.

clue.text: Island sports a kind of diver — but not beginner

indicators.note: the first letter of the diver word is left off

parts.note: a scuba diver uses breathing apparatus

explanation.surface: A Caribbean resort offers diving, though not for novices.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Soldier involved with girl, which is painful

indicators.note: the soldier is wrapped up inside the girl's name

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier's affair with a girl ends in heartache.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is a painful chest condition caused by poor blood supply to the heart.

clue.text: The setter usually goes off before this

definitions.text: The setter usually goes off before this

parts.words: The setter usually goes off before this
parts.note: reads as the crossword compiler leaving before the puzzle appears, but means a device whose timer is set and which then explodes, with its maker leaving first

explanation.definitionFit: A bomb fitted with a timer is set by its maker, who departs before it explodes.
